author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Massachusetts judge denied a request to release Janette MacAusland and dismiss the criminal case accusing her of killing her two children in their Wellesley home.

MacAusland, 49, is charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the April deaths of her 7-year-old son and 6-year-old daughter. She has pleaded not guilty. Her attorney argued that the available record was insufficient to continue holding her, while prosecutors said they are still awaiting the medical examiner’s final determination of the children’s causes and manners of death.

The judge rejected the defense motion and ordered MacAusland to remain held without bail. Authorities previously alleged that she traveled to a relative’s home in Vermont after the children were found and made incriminating statements to police. Those allegations have not been tested at trial.

The case remains at a pretrial stage, and the ruling does not determine guilt. Prosecutors must prove each charge beyond a reasonable doubt, and MacAusland retains the presumption of innocence. Further court proceedings are expected after the medical examiner completes the outstanding findings.
dek: A judge denied the defense request to release Janette MacAusland and dismiss the case while prosecutors await final medical-examiner findings.
headline: Judge keeps Wellesley mother held without bail in children’s deaths
